newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai feed mills actively seek April/May corn.
newsitem.headline: Thai feed mills actively seek April/May corn.

text.p: The Thai grains and oilseed market attracted brisk enquiry for corn this week after the cabinet approved a zero-tariff corn import quota of 200,000 tonnes for 1997, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Although the industry was still awaiting official allocation of the quota, most feed mills looked set to order if the right prices could be found, they said.
One major feed producer told Reuters he was seeking 50,000 tonnes of corn for April/May shipment, very likely from Argentina.

"We will also look at the United States and South Africa. The current prices are a bit expensive but I guess we need to order soon," he said."We might purchase at origin. But if the Argentine ports are congested, we might as well buy cargoes in transit."

Market sources confirmed that Thai conglomerate Charoen Pokphand had already booked two 50,000-tonne shipments of optional-origin corn from South America for March and April delivery. One of them was bought in December at US$130 per tonne.
Traders were sceptical about reports that Thailand may be buying 200,000 tonnes of corn from China. Non-WTO tariffs would have to be applied to such imports, making purchases unattractive.

"I must admit that the Chinese corn price is quite attractive and it has freight advantage. But with the high tariff and surcharge involved I'm not sure if the industry will be interested in such an option," said a trader from a U.S. house.
"But if they are in a hurry to meet a deadline, they might," he added.
The Thai government on Monday approved the 200,000-tonne corn import quota despite its forecast that the shortfall would be 345,000 tonnes.
The authorities said they expected the gap to be filled by local supplies that would become available by July. The deadline for the corn imports was the end of June.
The local corn price was indicated at 4.50 baht a kg from 4.40 baht a week earlier.
The soymeal market was relatively calmer with the industry waiting to see how upcoming local supplies would affect the price and watching Chicago movements before placing new orders.
